verdicts.title: Make accounting state fail closed across serialization, discretization, and composition
verdicts.rationale: All 7 children (#782-788) are closed-completed and every one is verifiable in the current tree at 12146ec4. Completion criteria clause by clause. verdicts.title: Correct DP-SGD sampling, adaptive-clipping, and accounting validation
verdicts.rationale: All 6 children (#798-803) are closed-completed and each is verifiable now. 'Adaptive clipping derives identical thresholds on every rank' — OPQ-309 is fixed: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-70 derives the collective schedule from the schema (`group_names = sorted(current_pg.values)`) and reduces `state._num_clipped[gname]` in that canonical order, and the per-group noise key at :76-78 is folded by the sorted index `i`, so the ordering no longer depends on how `_num_clipped` was built. I grepped every remaining `reduce_scalar` / `all_reduce` call site in packages/*/src — no other collective is driven by a rank-local dict iteration order. 'Invalid accounting parameters are rejected at construction and on deserialization' — OPQ-310 is fixed: `_adaclip.py:26-67` adds `AdaClip.__post_init__` (its comment names deserialization explicitly), rejecting `fraction_noise_std <= 0`, `expected_batch_size <= 0` and `num_groups < 1 or non-integral`, and normalising whole-float `num_groups`. I probed the sibling the finding flagged: `Gaussian(-1.0)` raises `ConfigurationError: noise_multiplier must be >= 0` and `Gaussian(0.0)` yields `epsilon_at = inf` — fail-closed. 'The runtime and accounting surfaces accept the same configurations' — OPQ-312 is fixed: `accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:49-58` now validates `0 < sample_rate <= 1` and the class docstring at :27-31 states `sample_rate=1.0` returns the base mechanism, matching the runtime sampler and `docs/user-guide/sampling.md:42,76,168`. OPQ-311 is fixed: every sampler now roots its stream under a namespaced tag — `POISSON_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.poisson"` (`sampling/_poisson.py:34,97`), `K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD` (`_k_out_of_t.py:26,55`), `CYCLIC_POISSON_STREAM_FOLD`, `B_MIN_SEP_STREAM_FOLD`, `BALLS_IN_BINS_STREAM_FOLD` in opaque-dpftrl. OPQ-356 is fixed: `num_groups` is now published in `docs/reference/accounting.md:312,321`, `docs/user-guide/accounting.md:179,182` and wired into the per-group recipe at `docs/user-guide/clipping.md:481,491`. verdicts.title: Restore patched-model fidelity to upstream
verdicts.rationale: Still real, and wider than the issue text. Open child #813 (OPQ-339) is unchanged in the current tree: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-102 still defines `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {gpt2, qwen3_next, deepseek_v4, gpt_oss}` and both `test_backward_grads_parity` (:278-279) and `test_vmap_grad_parity` (:483-484) still `pytest.skip` on it rather than `xfail(strict=True)`. I re-ran the suite with the skip set cleared on 12146ec4: `test_backward_grads_parity[gpt2]` fails with `transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01 (rtol=1e-05, atol=1e-06)` and `test_vmap_grad_parity[gpt2]` fails with it; `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` now PASS vmap-grad parity (2 passed), so two of the four exemptions are stale and only `qwen3_next` fails for the upstream reason the comment gives. Three corrections the issue text does not carry. (1) The umbrella's forward-parity clause has a second, independent hole no child covers: `test_parity.py:88-92` defines `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {deepseek_v4, gpt_oss, qwen3_next}` and `test_forward_logits_parity:251-252` skips them, so three registered families have no forward parity coverage at all — the criterion 'Every registered family passes forward ... parity against a genuinely unpatched reference' cannot be met as written and needs either an exemption mechanism or a rewording. (2) gpt2 is not an obscure corner: `supported_families()` returns it (verified by execution), and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/index.md:54` and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:21-23` use `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")` as the quick-start model while `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:180` lists GPT-2 in the compatibility matrix. #814's fail-closed signal for unregistered families does not fire because gpt2 IS registered. (3) The team added #898 as an eighth sub-issue (fused-kernel repeated-backward gap), which is tracked separately. Keep the umbrella, with the criteria corrected and the docs/registry consequence added to scope.
verdicts.corrected_title: Restore patched-model fidelity to upstream (gpt2 gradients, and the families with no parity reference)
verdicts.corrected_body:
## Goal

Guarantee that a patched model computes the same function as its upstream implementation, that the parity suite can prove it, and that no family the documentation promotes is silently exempt from that proof.

## Scope

Six of the original sub-issues are landed (#811, #812, #814, #815, #816, #817). What remains, re-scoped against the tree at 12146ec4:

- **#813 — grad-parity skips and the gpt2 mismatch.** `packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-102` still skips `gpt2`, `qwen3_next`, `deepseek_v4`, `gpt_oss` from `test_backward_grads_parity` (`:278-279`) and `test_vmap_grad_parity` (`:483-484`) with bare `pytest.skip`. Re-running with the set cleared shows the exemption list has rotted in three directions: `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` now **pass** vmap-grad parity; `qwen3_next` fails for the stated upstream reason (`masking_utils` data-dependent control flow under vmap); `gpt2` genuinely fails — `transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01` against `rtol=1e-05`.
- **New: the forward-parity hole.** `test_parity.py:88-92` also defines `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {deepseek_v4, gpt_oss, qwen3_next}`, and `test_forward_logits_parity:251-252` skips them, so three registered families have no forward-parity coverage either. No sub-issue covers this and the completion criteria as originally written cannot be satisfied for them.
- **New: gpt2 is promoted while unverified.** `supported_families()` includes `gpt2`, so `DPTrainer` patches it with no signal (#814's fail-closed path only covers *unregistered* families), and the user guide uses it as the quick-start model (`docs/user-guide/huggingface/index.md:54`, `dptrainer.md:21-23`) and lists it in the compatibility matrix (`model-patches.md:180`).
- **#898** (fused-kernel repeated-backward gap) is tracked as an added sub-issue.

## Completion criteria

- Every registered family either passes forward, gradient and vmap-gradient parity against a genuinely unpatched reference, **or** appears in a single reviewed exemption constant that names the reason and an issue number, is asserted by `test_parity_families_covered`, and is reflected in `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md`.
- No parity exemption uses bare `pytest.skip`: each is `pytest.param(..., marks=pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...))` so a family that starts passing fails the suite.
- `gpt2` either passes gradient and vmap-gradient parity, or is removed from `supported_families()` and from the quick-start examples and compatibility matrix.

This is a tracking issue; implementation belongs in its independently closable sub-issues.

Audit source: OPQ-339.

verdicts.corrected_title: Restore auditing statistical validity: bound v_k for truncated ranks
verdicts.corrected_body:
## Goal

Make the one-run μ-GDP surface usable at its own documented scale, or honest about where it stops working.

## Scope

Three of the four sub-issues are landed and verified at 12146ec4:

- #829 — `one_run/_estimate.py:44` raises `_MIN_GRID_SIZE` to `1_000` and `:192-194` rejects coarser grids (OPQ-351).
- #830 — `attacks/_helpers.py:159-175` records `CoinFlip.dataset_size`, checks it against `len(dataset)` and bounds-checks the canary indices before building the scoring loader (OPQ-352).
- #831 — the stale "Bonferroni (default)" comment is gone (OPQ-353).

Only **#828** remains, and it is unchanged: `one_run/_gdp.py:41` still pins `_MAX_EXACT_RANKS = 2000`, `:336-338` pins every rank past that at `v_k = 0.5`, and `:385-397` folds `n_trunc * 0.5` into the Chernoff expectation, so no finite μ lifts the p-value to significance once the attack is strong enough. `:88-91` raises rather than returning a bound. The cap is documented nowhere: `docs/user-guide/auditing.md` and `docs/reference/auditing.md` contain no occurrence of `2000`, `truncat` or `_MAX_EXACT`, while the guide's own canary-count table recommends 10^4 and above.

## Completion criteria

- A strong attack at the guide's recommended canary count returns a μ̂/ε estimate rather than raising, via a μ-dependent upper bound on `v_k` for truncated ranks.
- Failing that (the fallback #828 itself names as the minimum): the rank truncation, the attack strength at which the estimator stops converging, and the recommended workaround are documented on both auditing pages, and the raised error points at them.

This is a tracking issue; implementation belongs in #828.

Audit source: OPQ-350, OPQ-351, OPQ-352, OPQ-353.

verdicts.title: Close CI fail-open gates and restore test integrity
verdicts.rationale: The second completion-criteria clause is met; the first is not, and it was deliberately declined rather than missed — the issue text must say so instead of claiming an unmet bar. Met: 'no blocking lane can pass on an unavailable accelerator' — 039fc012 (#876) added `.github/scripts/assert_cuda_available.sh`, invoked both from python-tests.yml:142-143 and defensively from run_python_test_package.sh:14; it keys off the marker expression, strips `not cuda` first, and does a real device round-trip rather than trusting `is_available()` (OPQ-377). verdicts.corrected_title: Close CI fail-open gates and restore test integrity (residual: kernel CUDA markers)
verdicts.corrected_body:
## Goal

Ensure the lanes that are supposed to block a regression can actually fail, and that the suite can detect the defect classes the re-audit found.

## Scope

Landed and verified at 12146ec4:

- #832 — `.github/scripts/assert_cuda_available.sh`, called from `python-tests.yml:142-143` and again from `run_python_test_package.sh:14`; it keys off the marker expression rather than the runner label and reads a value back off the device (OPQ-377).
- #833 — `packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py` now ties realized RMS noise to `noise_stddev` within six sampling standard errors and asserts a 0.97x perturbation fails; `packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_realized_stddev.py` covers the MF row-norm path (OPQ-379).
- #834, #835, #837, #838, #839, #840, #842 — all landed.

**Declined, with residual risk recorded rather than left implicit:**

- #836 (closed not-planned). `allow-empty-test-selection: true` remains on the distributed lane (`.github/workflows/pr.yml:81`) and the three CUDA lanes (`:145`, `:160`, `:177`), and `run_python_test_package.sh:43-46` turns pytest's exit 5 into exit 0 under it. `python-tests-distributed` is a required input to the blocking `python-tests` gate (`pr.yml:190-203`), whose jq filter (`:207-222`) only excuses `skipped` for `python-tests-cuda*`. **Residual risk:** a marker rename, a collection break, or a deleted `distributed`/`cuda` marker that drops a required lane to zero collected tests still leaves the gate green. The CUDA preflight from #832 catches an unavailable device but not an empty selection on an available one.
- #841 (closed not-planned). No lane exercises Python 3.12, which every wheel advertises. **Residual risk:** a 3.12-only incompatibility ships undetected.

**Open:** #880 — restore CUDA marker coverage for the LoRA and linear-cross-entropy kernel tests.

## Completion criteria

- #880 lands, so the kernel tests it names are selected by the CUDA lanes.
- The two declines above are recorded in the CI documentation (or as a comment next to each `allow-empty-test-selection: true`) so the next reader does not mistake the flag for an oversight; re-opening either is a deliberate decision, not a bug report.

This is a tracking issue; implementation belongs in its independently closable sub-issues.

Separately, the umbrella's first completion clause needs correcting: the executable-docs gate that landed (pr.yml:285-300, from 12146ec4 / #1034) runs `examples/quickstart.py`, `python -m doctest` on one façade module, and three tutorial notebooks — it does not execute the Markdown snippets in `docs/user-guide/` or `docs/reference/`, which is what 'every documented snippet executes in CI' meant, and which is the gap #775's own note predicted.
verdicts.corrected_title: Reconcile citations with their sources (Sweep C) and close the executable-docs gap
verdicts.corrected_body:
## Goal

Bring published documentation, reference tables and scholarly citations back into agreement with the code, and make the agreement mechanically checkable so it does not drift again.

## Scope

Sweeps A (#843) and B (#844) are closed. Sweep C (**#845**) is open and, checked against 12146ec4, five of its six findings are present verbatim — the manual-pass failure mode this issue's own note warned about:

- OPQ-371 — `packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/_schedule_free.py:10`: `Defazio, Yaida, Cutkosky` — "Yaida" is not an author of arXiv:2405.15682 (it reads as a corruption of "Yang"). Sole repo-wide hit.
- OPQ-372a — `alignment/dpo/loss/_discopop.py:6-7` and `:41` attribute DiscoPOP to Azar et al. / NeurIPS 2024; DiscoPOP is Lu et al., arXiv:2406.08414, and Azar et al. is IPO.
- OPQ-372b — `alignment/logprob/_sequence.py:15-16` says the `ld_alpha` split "is not implemented here" while `sequence_logp` accepts (`:37`), documents (`:54-62`) and implements it (`:82-95`); only the fused path lacks it (`:134`).
- OPQ-373 — `amplification/truncated_poisson.rs:18,124` (and `packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_cross_validation.py:460`) cite the key `[Gan25]`, which is defined nowhere. The dataset-size-dependent adjacency the guarantee assumes is still undocumented.
- OPQ-374 — `docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:62` and `matrix_factorization/lambda_cgd.rs:8,65,130` cite "Theorem 1, eq 15"; eq (15) is a utility quantity and Theorem 1's Toeplitz hypothesis does not cover the default `normalized=True` path (Lemma 8 / eq (12) does).
- OPQ-375 — `dpftrl/sampling/_balls_in_bins.py:26` and `accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:46` give only arXiv:2412.16802, which contains neither "Definition 3.1" nor "Lemma 3.2"; those are in arXiv:2410.06266.

Done: OPQ-376's validation half — `dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:660-663` now enforces `0.0 <= momentum < 1.0`. Its documentation half (α pinned to 1) is still open: the note exists at `_bisr.py:235` but not in `docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md`.

**Correction to the first completion clause.** The executable-docs gate that landed (`.github/workflows/pr.yml:285-300`, #1034) runs `examples/quickstart.py`, `python -m doctest` on `packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`, and three tutorial notebooks. It does **not** execute the Markdown snippets under `docs/user-guide/` or `docs/reference/`, so "every documented snippet executes in CI" is not yet true.

## Completion criteria

- Every citation in source and docs resolves to a record whose stated result covers the use made of it, verified from a **generated** per-file checklist rather than a manual pass.
- The Markdown snippets under `docs/user-guide/` and `docs/reference/` execute in CI, not only the tutorial notebooks and the quickstart script.
- Every published default is generated from, or checked against, its dataclass.

This is a tracking issue; implementation belongs in #845 and a follow-up for the Markdown-snippet gate.

Audit source: OPQ-371, OPQ-372, OPQ-373, OPQ-374, OPQ-375, OPQ-376.

findings.title: GPT-2 is the documented quick-start model and a listed compatible family, but its per-example gradients diverge from upstream by 53x relative error
findings.claim: `supported_families()` includes `gpt2` (verified by execution), so `DPTrainer` auto-patches a GPT-2 model on construction with no signal — #814's fail-closed path only fires for *unregistered* families. The documentation promotes exactly that family: `docs/user-guide/huggingface/index.md:54` and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:21-23` both use `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")` as the quick-start model, and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:180` lists `| GPT-2 | 124M, 355M | ... |` in the compatibility matrix. Meanwhile the parity suite excludes gpt2 from both gradient tests by name (`packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-102`, skipped at `:278-279` and `:483-484`), and the exclusion hides a live mismatch, not roundoff. The docs carry no caveat: grep over `docs/` for 'gpt2' returns only the three promotional sites, none of which mentions gradient parity.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows the HF quick start verbatim — `DPTrainer` on `gpt2` with `privacy_target_epsilon=8.0` — and trains. `apply_model_patches` fires because gpt2 is registered, so there is no warning. The per-example gradients `vmap(grad(...))` feeds into `clipped_grad` differ materially from the model's true gradients, so the model optimizes a different objective than advertised. Clipping still bounds sensitivity, so the reported epsilon stays valid, but the training result is silently wrong. Reproduced on the current tree (12146ec4) by clearing `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and re-running the shipped tests: `test_backward_grads_parity[gpt2]` fails with `transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01 (rtol=1e-05, atol=1e-06)` and `test_vmap_grad_parity[gpt2]` fails likewise.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:278-279 and :483-484 — `if family in _GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES: pytest.skip(f"{family} has unreliable gradient parity")`

Executed on 12146ec4 with the skip set cleared via a pytest plugin: `AssertionError: gpt2: backward grad transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01 (rtol=1e-05, atol=1e-06)`; both gpt2 grad tests FAILED while `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` PASSED vmap-grad parity in the same run

`uv run python -c "from opaque.api.patches.transformers.models import apply_gpt2_patches; from opaque.api.patches.transformers._registry import supported_families; print('gpt2' in supported_families())"` → True
docs/user-guide/huggingface/dptrainer.md:21-23 — same model in the trainer walkthrough
findings.fix_sketch: Either fix the gpt2 backward path (the skip comment blames the kv_cache/batchify patches), or de-register `gpt2` from `supported_families()` and replace it in the quick start and `dptrainer.md` with a family that passes gradient parity (llama, qwen2, mistral all do) and remove or footnote its compatibility-matrix row. In the interim, add a row-level caveat in `model-patches.md` naming the families excluded from gradient parity, and have #813 convert the skips to `xfail(strict=True)` so the exclusion cannot rot.

findings.title: Three registered families have no forward-parity coverage either, a hole no child of #769 covers
findings.claim: OPQ-339 and its child #813 are scoped to the *gradient* skips. The same test module carries a second, independent exemption set for the forward test: `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {"deepseek_v4", "gpt_oss", "qwen3_next"}` at :88-92, applied by `test_forward_logits_parity` at :251-252 with `pytest.skip(f"{family} requires runtime compatibility shims")`. Combined with `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES`, these three families have **no** parity coverage at all — not forward, not backward, not vmap-grad — while `test_parity_families_covered` (:508-520) only subtracts the one-element `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and therefore reports them as covered. #769's completion criterion ('Every registered family passes forward, gradient, and vmap-gradient parity against a genuinely unpatched reference') is stated for forward parity too, and no sub-issue addresses it.
findings.failure_scenario: A patch regression that changes `deepseek_v4`, `gpt_oss` or `qwen3_next` forward logits — a rebind of the wrong attention forward, a dropped softcap, a mis-scaled RoPE — is invisible to the parity suite, which reports these families as covered because the coverage guard cannot see either skip set. The user gets wrong logits and wrong gradients with no test signal. That said, the skip reason is partly legitimate for these three: the unpatched reference itself needs runtime shims, so a 'genuinely unpatched' reference may not exist — which is why the criterion needs an explicit exemption mechanism rather than silence.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:86-92 — `# These families require runtime compatibility shims even for an ordinary forward, so no strict-upstream parity reference is available.` / `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {"deepseek_v4", "gpt_oss", "qwen3_next"}`
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:251-252 — `if family in _STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES: pytest.skip(f"{family} requires runtime compatibility shims")`

packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:508-520 — `test_parity_families_covered` subtracts only `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (a one-element set: `qwen3_5_moe`), so neither skip set is visible to the guard
`git log -S"_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES"` → 5936552b only: the hole shipped with the suite itself and no delta commit touched it
findings.fix_sketch: Merge both skip sets into one reviewed `_PARITY_EXEMPTIONS: dict[str, str]` mapping family → reason-with-issue-number, assert in `test_parity_families_covered` that every exempt family is in it, and surface the list in `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md` so a reader can see which families are not parity-verified. Convert the per-test guards to `xfail(strict=True)` where a reference does exist.

findings.title: tree_leaves silently returns [] for Opaque wrapper types, the last survivor of the OPQ-333 wrapper-blindness class in the same public facade
findings.claim: The #806 fix made `global_norm` raise `InputTypeError` when handed a `ClippedPytree`/`NoisedPytree`/`SecondMomentClippingOutput`/`SecondMomentNoiseOutput` (pytree.py:377-400), naming `.pytree` as the explicit numerical view. Its neighbour in the same module and the same `__all__` was not given the same treatment: `tree_leaves` (:112-129) does `flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]`, and because the wrappers are unregistered frozen dataclasses they flatten to a single non-tensor leaf and are filtered out. Verified by execution: `tree_leaves(clipped({"g": torch.tensor([3.0,4.0])}, max_norm=1.0))` returns `[]`, while `tree_flatten` on the same object returns `([ClippedPytree(...)], PyTreeSpec(*))`.
findings.failure_scenario: A user logging gradient statistics writes `sum(p.square().sum() for p in tree_leaves(grads)).sqrt()` (the obvious hand-rolled form of the norm `global_norm` now refuses) and gets `0.0` forever, or `torch.stack(tree_leaves(grads))` and gets an empty-list error at a confusing call site. No exception, no warning. Utility/observability only — the misuse never reduces noise or raises sensitivity, so epsilon is unaffected.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:111-129 — `def tree_leaves(tree): flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]`
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:377-400 — `global_norm` raises `InputTypeError` for the same four wrapper types (the #806/OPQ-333 fix)

Executed on 12146ec4: `tree_leaves(clipped({'g': torch.tensor([3.0,4.0])}, max_norm=1.0))` → `[]`; `global_norm(...)` on the same value → `InputTypeError: ClippedPytree global norm is unsupported ...`
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/pytree.py:1-31 — both names are exported from the same public facade
findings.fix_sketch: Give `tree_leaves` (and `tree_flatten` / `tree_flatten_with_paths` / `partition`, which share the behaviour) the same guard as `global_norm`: raise `InputTypeError` naming `.pytree`, or unwrap the DP wrappers before flattening. A one-line shared `_reject_dp_wrapper(tree)` helper covers all of them and keeps the facade internally consistent.
